speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing this sudden vertigo, and does the spinning sensation worsen when you move your head or change position?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any new hearing loss, tinnitus, or a feeling of fullness in your ear alongside the vertigo? Also, have you noticed any weakness, numbness, slurred speech, or double vision since the episode started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. I am scared this situation could become urgent and I need the most appropriate final answer immediately. Please do not wait too long before committing to a next step.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The history of brief (3-minute) vertigo triggered by position change, without auditory or neurological deficits, is classic for displaced otoconial crystals in the semicircular canals.
